title: चिकित्सकको भाषा {The language of the physician}
nepali: ‘चिकित्सकको भाषा’ शीर्षकको प्रस्तुत अध्ययन पाँच जना चिकित्सकले बिरामीसँग प्रयोग गरेको भाषामा आधारित रहेर गरिएको अध्ययन हो । यस अध्ययनबाट चिकित्सकीय भाषाका वाक्यहरू प्रायजसो छोटो र सम्प्रेषणजन्य हुने गरेको देखियो । उनीहरूको भाषामा पनि कथ्य भाषामा पाइने लोपगत विशेषताहरूयुक्त प्रयोग भएको पाइयो । उनीहरूले भाषामा कोड मिश्रण र चिकित्सा शब्दावलीको अत्यधिक प्रयोग गर्ने गरेका हुनाले सर्वसाधारणका लागि सहज बोधगम्य हुन नसकेको अवस्था विद्यमान रहेको छ । यही कोड मिश्रण र चिकित्सा शब्दावलीको प्रयोगले गर्दा चिकित्सकको भाषामा सम्प्रेषणगत जटिलताको सिर्जना हुन गई विचार विनिमयमा सहज नभएको देखिन्छ । चिकित्सकको भाषालाई सर्वसाधारणका लागि सम्प्रेषण योग्य बनाउनका लागि उनीहरूको अभिव्यक्तिमा सकेसम्म नेपाली शब्दको प्रयोग गरी कोड मिश्रणयुक्त प्रयोगलाई न्यूनीकरण गर्न आवश्यक छ । यसका लागि चिकित्सक र सर्वसाधारणलाई चिकित्साशास्त्रीय नेपाली को ज्ञान दिनाले सम्प्रेषणका लागि सहज वातावरण निर्माण हुने सक्नेछ ।
american_english: ‘The Language of the Physician’ is a study based on the language five doctors use when talking to patients. The study found that medical language sentences are often short and meant to communicate. Their language also includes features of discourse language that are missing. They use a lot of code-mixing and medical terminology in their language, which makes it hard for ordinary people to understand. This code-mixing and use of medical terminology creates complexity in communication, making it difficult to exchange ideas. To make medical language easier to communicate for ordinary people, doctors should use Nepali words as much as possible and reduce code-mixing. If doctors and ordinary people learn medical Nepali, it will create an easy environment for communication.

informal_english: The article 'The Language of the Physician' looks at how five doctors talk to their patients. It found that doctors' language is pretty short and straightforward, meant to get things across clearly. But their speech also misses out on some key bits of normal conversation. They throw in a lot of mixed languages and medical jargon, which makes it tough for regular folks to understand. This mix of languages and technical terms creates communication headaches, making it hard to really connect and share ideas. To make doctor talk more accessible for everyone, physicians should try using more Nepali words and cut back on the language mixing. If both doctors and patients learned some medical Nepali, it would create a much smoother communication environment for everyone.
